task_instance: Build a minimal Fireflies contract-safe CI lane for a sample repo: a named GraphQL transcripts query document, a synthetic success fixture, Webhook V2 HMAC test vectors (valid, tampered body, malformed signature, duplicate event), an offline deterministic test file doing GraphQL syntax validation + HMAC verification + secret scanning, and a GitHub Actions workflow that runs the offline lane and gates the live lane behind environment approval.
blocker_detail: The skill's core deliverable is a verification/CI lane whose value is deterministic test EXECUTION: static GraphQL validation (needs a GraphQL parser such as graphql-core), Webhook V2 HMAC vector checks (needs running hmac/sha256 to compute and compare signatures - the fixtures intentionally mark expected signatures as computed at runtime), secret-scan assertions, and a pytest run. The skill's own Validation section requires rerunning the smallest deterministic check before reporting success. The office-assistant runtime cannot run code, install packages, or run pytest, so the authored lane cannot be executed or verified. HMAC signature correctness in particular cannot be confirmed by reading alone.
evidence: Read SKILL.md and its references file (the references list is entirely unreachable placeholders, and web fetch is disallowed this round). Authored a complete sample lane under the work directory sample-repo/: graphql/transcripts.graphql (named query), fixtures/transcripts_success.json (synthetic success), fixtures/webhook_v2_vectors.json (4 HMAC vectors), tests/test_contract.py (offline GraphQL parse via graphql-core + HMAC verification + fixture-shape + secret-scan assertions), and .github/workflows/fireflies-ci.yml (offline job + approval-gated live job). Files authored successfully as text. Verification blocked: running the deterministic checks (pytest, graphql-core parse, hmac.compare_digest over the vectors) requires code execution and package installation, neither of which the runtime grants; the webhook vectors' expected signatures are only knowable by executing HMAC-SHA256. No credentials, network, or MCP/connector tools were used; the GraphQL endpoint host is only referenced via an env var, never written literally.
